note.question: Can a ranking publisher profitably create uncertainty through its methodology so that consumers pay for a report that is less informative about intrinsic product quality?
note.overview: A product expert strategically commits to a ranking methodology before a consumer decides whether to buy the resulting report and which product to select. The paper explicitly characterizes pure-strategy perfect Bayesian equilibria, contrasts expertand consumer-optimal equilibrium selections, and tests those predictions in a laboratory game.

source.quote: Related Literature Our study relates to two separate strands of literature: in terms of the subject matter, product rankings and more generally non–seller-provided product informa­ tion; in terms of the theory and experiment, strategic information transmission.
Setup There are two players, a product expert (he) and a con­ sumer (she), and two products, A and B.
Online product reviews submitted by con­ sumers, for example, in physician ratings (Lu and Rui 2018), have been shown to provide useful product infor­ mation.
Unlike our game, however, there is no element of selling information in Bayesian persuasion.

models.method: The authors solve a two-player Bayesian ranking-report game, identify acquisition, consumer-optimal, and expert-optimal equilibrium predictions, discretize the ranking-method space for the laboratory, and test comparative predictions across four between-subject treatments using choice frequencies, nonparametric comparisons, and random-effects logit models.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The expert first publicly commits to a ranking method β before observing the realized intrinsic value of Product B. The consumer observes the method and decides whether to pay fee f for the report. Nature's product value and the report outcome determine the available information; after seeing the report when acquired, or only the committed method otherwise, the consumer selects Product A or B. The expert chooses how noisy and potentially misleading the ranking will be before the uncertain product value is realized.

components.label: Pure-strategy perfect Bayesian equilibrium with expert-optimal and consumer-optimal selections
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Pure-strategy perfect Bayesian equilibrium with expert-optimal and consumer-optimal selections. Proposition 1 states that the expert selects a method satisfying G(β_0)≥f whenever one exists, after which consumer report acquisition and product choice are sequentially rational under Bayes-consistent beliefs. The paper then selects among the expert's payoff-equivalent report-selling methods by maximizing either consumer utility or willingness to pay.
